assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of the Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state opened a whole class of materials, followed by a decisive experimental observation of edge-channel conductance in HgTe wells. A clear case of an original prediction plus an original experiment, with lasting impact on materials physics and device concepts.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical contributions; Molenkamp's group did the first experimental realization (with Zhang's theory proposal for HgTe not in the supplied credit, which complicates a fair account). Three names are a natural configuration, though Bernevig/Hughes/Zhang and the 3D-TI experimentalists are unrepresented here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over about two decades across HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 and related materials, including ARPES and transport; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit omits the HgTe quantum-well proposal and the 3D topological insulator discovery, which the committee would need to weigh.
Overlap with the QAH candidate may require a decision on how to split topological recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (magic-wavelength trapping) delivered a new regime of frequency metrology, reaching 10^-18 uncertainty and opening a door to tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. It is an invention with clear and verified performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realized the first Sr lattice clock; Ye's group brought the clock to record accuracy and many-body regimes. Two laureates is a clean configuration; Ye already shares the 2005 prize for the frequency comb, which is not a barrier but needs thought. Other contributors (e.g. Ludlow, Lemonde, Takamoto) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many national labs and compared across continents; performance is verified and still improving. Redefinition of the second is pending but the invention is mature enough now.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should wait for the SI second redefinition.
Ye's prior prize and the weight of the broader JILA program.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in 1995 made magnetic tunnel junctions practical, underlying hard-drive read heads and MRAM. It is an original experiment with enormous technological and scientific consequence, closely matching the criterion of discovery that benefits humanity.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently and nearly simultaneously reported reproducible room-temperature TMR in 1995, which I regard as the original experiments. Parkin's later MgO-based high-TMR work is a major improvement, so the question of the second, better demonstration arises; I would not credit it first. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature result is prior art not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: widespread independent confirmation and decades of industrial use. The 2007 prize for GMR is adjacent, which may affect perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
Whether Parkin's MgO advance should count as the decisive step versus the original 1995 observation.
Prior art by Julliere is outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field, giving a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Major new door-opening, with a rare close link between prediction and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative magic-angle prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This is a natural three-person configuration, though the contribution of Cao as lead experimentalist and of earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. Reasonably mature experimentally, less so in interpretation.
uncertainties: Unsettled microscopic origin of superconductivity.
Prior theoretical work on twisted-bilayer flat bands may bear on credit.
Possibly somewhat early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single nitrogen-vacancy centers and coherent spin control at room temperature established a robust solid-state quantum system and a new class of nanoscale sensors for magnetic field, temperature and biology. A tool that lets us see things previously inaccessible.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group first detected single NV spins optically (1997) and Jelezko and Wrachtrup demonstrated coherent control (2004). Lukin contributed major theoretical and later experimental advances, including quantum registers and sensing protocols, but the originality of the first observation points to Wrachtrup and Jelezko.
assessment.maturity: Broadly verified and in wide use, with growing commercial and biological applications. Sensing impact is real but still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin or Awschalom-type work should share the credit; Lukin is in the supplied names, but I weight the first demonstration more.
Overlap with other solid-state spin and quantum information candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in LaFeAsO(1-x)F(x), then up to 55 K, revealed a second family of high-Tc superconductors and reframed thinking about unconventional pairing. The result is original, clearly measured and widely confirmed.
assessment.attribution: The original discovery was published by Hosono's group in 2008 (Kamihara et al.). Chen and Zhao's groups quickly raised Tc and found new compounds, which is important follow-up but in my reading is second-wave work. I propose Hosono alone, as the credited list allows.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in thousands of papers; the pairing mechanism is still unsettled, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is acceptable though it is nearly two decades old.
uncertainties: Unresolved mechanism of superconductivity.
Whether Chen and Zhao's rapid advances count as decisive contributions.
Co-discoverer credit within Hosono's group is not visible in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets, first seen by neutron scattering and then imaged in real space by Lorentz TEM, showed topological spin textures with emergent electrodynamics and ultralow current-driven motion. As a microscopist, I value that real-space imaging confirmed it directly.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group provided the initial 2009 discovery, Tokura's group the real-space imaging and thin-film work, and Rosch the theory of emergent electrodynamics and current-driven motion. The theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and colleagues is not in the credited names, which leaves a significant attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, including room-temperature skyrmions, but technological applications are still prospective. Fairly mature scientifically, less so for societal benefit.
uncertainties: Bogdanov's prior prediction is absent from the credited names.
Applications to racetrack memory remain unproven.
Overlap of Tokura with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a nonzero theta-13 by reactor antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay and RENO completed the three-flavor mixing picture and enabled searches for CP violation. A clean, verifiable experimental discovery of clear importance for understanding nature.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) delivered the decisive 2012 results, with Double Chooz and T2K as close competitors and the 2012 results arriving nearly simultaneously. The distinction of spokespersons versus the large collaborations is a recurrent difficulty for fair attribution.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several experiments and continually refined. The discovery is mature and stable, and two neutrino prizes (2002, 2015) already exist, so novelty might be questioned.
uncertainties: Credit boundaries across Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K are contested.
Possible fatigue after the 2015 neutrino oscillation prize.
Large-collaboration credit assignment.
